field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Start with a basal leaf: curly dock has long, narrow blades with conspicuously crisped/wavy margins. Follow the stem to the papery ocrea at a leaf node, then check the mature fruiting valves. Wavy leaves alone are not a definitive identification.
vegetative_checkpoints: Erect perennial with a basal rosette and tall flowering stem; record plant height with a scale.
Alternate stem leaves; look for the membranous ocrea wrapping each node, characteristic of Polygonaceae.
Basal leaf blades often roughly 10–40 cm long, narrower than broadleaf dock, with strongly undulating margins; measure complete blade rather than guessing from photographs.
reproductive_checkpoints: Dense branching clusters of small flowers becoming rusty-brown fruiting clusters.
At maturity inspect the three enlarged inner perianth segments (fruiting valves), typically about 3.5–6 mm long; record their outline and tubercles.
Check three-angled achenes (roughly 2–3 mm); a millimeter-scale macro is required for confident comparisons.

look_alikes.difference: Often fiddle-shaped basal leaves and toothed mature fruiting-valve margins; do not rely on leaf outline alone.
Broadleaf dock has broader, blunt-based leaves; compare mature valves and tubercles.
Narrow-leaved dock can overlap vegetatively; use mature fruit-valve characters and regional evidence.
